name: Pattern Alchemy
description: A workshop album for the newest parts of the language. Every sketch names its own functions (as methods, as function values, through apply, as pattern builders, with defaults and with functions as arguments) and leans on the standard library: within, chunk, zoom, compress, fastGap, linger, brak, press, swingBy, echo and superimpose; seeded shuffles, scrambles and cycle choices; arithmetic that grows melodies from counting; and the new scales, from hirajoshi and in sen to hungarian minor, whole tone and lydian dominant. Read the comments: each sketch explains the trick it plays.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Hirajoshi Garden
sketches.description: Two kotos built from one function and one phrase builder, rising and falling through the hirajoshi scale, under a legato shakuhachi, water and a temple bell.

sketches.name: Canon Engine
sketches.description: A theme written once as scale degrees; a function turns it into each entry of a three-voice canon, another dresses every entry as a bowed string, over a ground bass and an echoing harpsichord.

sketches.name: Ratchet Lab
sketches.description: Acid techno built from two tiny functions: one that takes another function and stacks a changed copy, and a ratchet used as a method value, a partial application and through apply.

sketches.name: Break Surgery
sketches.description: Drum and bass cut up live: one break, dealt back in new orders with shuffle, rebuilt with repeats by scramble, held on its first quarter by linger, with brak stabs and a pressed bass.

sketches.name: Hungarian Dance
sketches.description: A csárdás in A hungarian minor: a fiddle and a cimbalom each defined once as a function, an accented oom-pah, and a band that rushes every eighth bar with hurry.

sketches.name: Number Garden
sketches.description: Melodies grown from plain arithmetic: counting by threes modulo eight, halving and rounding down, even-only random degrees, rounded smooth noise and a sine squeezed into a narrow pan.
sketches.source:
setcpm(96/4)

// run(8).mul(3).mod(8) gives 0 3 6 1 4 7 2 5: every step once, in leaps
// The pan is a sine made bipolar, scaled by .4 and mapped back, so it sways from .3 to .7
leaps: n(run(8).mul(3).mod(8)).scale("F:lydian").transpose(12)
  .s("triangle").timbre("glass").decay(.3).sustain(0).release(.5)
  .pan(sine.toBipolar().mul(.4).fromBipolar())
  .delay(.3).delaytime(3/16).gain(.22)

// run(8).div(2).floor() gives 0 0 1 1 2 2 3 3: the same count, each step twice, an octave down
steps: n(run(8).div(2).floor()).scale("F:lydian").sub(12)
  .s("sawtooth").lpf(900).decay(.2).sustain(.3).release(.1).gain(.26)

// irand(4).mul(2) picks only even degrees, so every bell is a chord tone
bells: n(irand(4).mul(2).segment(4)).scale("F:lydian").transpose(12)
  .s("sine").fm(2).fmh(2.76).decay(1).sustain(0).release(1.2).seed("even").room(.6).gain(.16)

// Smooth noise, rounded into scale steps and thinned out
wander: n(perlin.range(-2, 6).segment(16).round()).scale("F:lydian").transpose(24)
  .degradeBy(.5).seed("numbers")
  .s("sine").decay(.1).sustain(0).release(.3).pan(rand).room(.5).gain(.1)

// ceil lifts a slow sine onto whole-number degrees for the pad's root
root: n(sine.range(0, 3).segment(2).ceil()).scale("F:lydian").octave(-1).slow(2)
  .s("sine").attack(.5).sustain(.8).release(1).gain(.3)
pad: note("[f3,a3,c4,e4]").slow(4).s("sawtooth").unison(3).detune(.2)
  .attack(2).release(3).lpf(1200).room(.7).gain(.12)

drums: s("bd ~ ~ bd ~ ~ bd ~, ~ ~ rim ~").lpf(3000).gain(.32)

sketches.name: Whole-Tone Dream
sketches.description: One run up the whole-tone scale, reshaped four ways: a halo passed as a function value, a second half that plays the first backwards, a zoomed middle, a compressed bass and a clock that only ticks half the time.

sketches.name: Lydian Dominant Lift
sketches.description: Funk in G lydian dominant: swung drums with swingBy, a bass that sits a hair behind the beat with nudge and plays short with legato, pushed chords with press, and a lead with seeded flourishes.

sketches.name: Egyptian Night
sketches.description: A singer defined once as a function with a voice-type default: an alto sings a syllable line in the egyptian pentatonic, a tenor answers below, and a choir, a hum and a frame drum hold the night.

sketches.name: Seed Garden
sketches.description: A generative garden in E in sen: one seeded melody shared by two hands, thinned by degradeBy and undegradeBy, ornamented by often and rarely, with bells that choose whole cycles to hurry. Change the seed for a new garden.
